final.remaining_skew: Moderate upside as the company executes the $5.5bn cost savings target against a challenged streaming margin profile [D03; D04]
final.next_catalyst_and_timing: Operational execution of the announced cost program and clarity on the strategic role of ESPN and Hulu [D03; D05]

drivers.driver: The September support agreement provided a board seat and governance input, necessitating a period of holding to evaluate management's execution of the strategic plan [D03; D05].
Management has initiated a significant $5.5 billion cost-savings program, which is a critical step toward the operational turnaround we originally envisioned [D03].
Direct-to-consumer operating losses have widened, placing pressure on the core business model and making the achievement of streaming profitability a primary performance hurdle [D03].

final.memo:
We maintain our position in Disney as the company enters a crucial phase of operational restructuring. Following our private engagement, the September support agreement successfully secured a board seat, which provides us with institutional influence to monitor and guide management’s capital allocation and strategic priorities [D03; D07]. The current priority is to hold and observe the execution of the recently announced $5.5 billion cost-savings program, which addresses one of the key pillars of our initial thesis [D03].

While the company’s revenue grew 7.8% in Q1 FY2023, the underlying margin pressure in the direct-to-consumer segment—where losses worsened by approximately $0.5 billion—highlights the scale of the challenge in transitioning to a streaming-first model [D03; D06]. We are closely watching how management balances the necessary reinvestment in streaming against the secular decline in linear networks, particularly within the ESPN portfolio, which remains a complex asset linked to broader distribution and advertising economics [D01; D05].

Our standstill obligations under the current governance agreement restrict further public agitation at this time, aligning our interests with a disciplined evaluation of the board’s progress [D03; D05]. We remain focused on whether these operating actions will meaningfully improve cash conversion and shareholder value over the next 1-3 years. If the company fails to deliver on these commitments, or if the streaming economics prove permanently impaired despite our intervention, we will reassess our capital commitment without hesitation [D05; D08].
